name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
short_desc: The Soviet Union dissolves as its republics become independent states, ending a central institution of the Cold War order.
location: Soviet Union · Moscow · Russia · Ukraine · Belarus · Armenia · Azerbaijan · Georgia (country) · Estonia · Latvia · Lithuania · Kazakhstan · Kyrgyzstan · Tajikistan · Turkmenistan · Uzbekistan · Moldova
date_note: Declarations and negotiations unfolded throughout 1991. Gorbachev resigned on 25 December; remaining Soviet institutions formally acknowledged dissolution on 26 December. Successor conflicts continued.
notes: Added after a catalog gap review on 24 October 2026. A world-order transition distinct from the fall of the Berlin Wall, the Cold War period and the Soviet state’s existence span. Evidence and date rationale: Republic declarations and negotiations unfolded throughout 1991. Gorbachev resigned on 25 December and the remaining Soviet institutions formally acknowledged dissolution on 26 December. This point is the final state dissolution, not the whole reform process or a claim that every successor conflict ended. Primary evidence: https://www.bush41library.gov/digital-research-room/finding-aid/foia/records-dissolution-soviet-union. Cached Wikipedia introduction and lead image provide separately attributed background. Remains review, not comprehensive factual approval.
